note: THE FIRST RUNS OF THE GAME-DATA TOOLS ON THE MACHINE THAT HAS GAME DATA. 62 of the 100 scripts in `scripts/debug/` read game data and the phone is the only machine holding any; they became reachable on 2026-09-06 (`phone_run debug`) and none had ever been run. NOT TIMINGS: every figure here is a COUNT of what a tool read out of the authored data. Two of the first three tools died before printing anything — on a DIRECTORY the phone does not have, read unguarded — which is the finding this row exists for.
device: MGA-LX3 / Termux, node v24.18.0, the 2/03 phone
tree: game-src/original on the phone — NOT verified to be the copy earlier baselines were taken on (see datOrderCheck.rowsDisagreeWithDoc)

datOrderCheck.what: Does any text `inst` row place a model whose IDE `gta.dat` lists later? Stock must be 0.
datOrderCheck.rowsDisagreeWithDoc: docs/debug/README.md recorded 9 268 rows for this same path. Same verdict, different COUNT — so the two runs read different copies of `game-src/original` rather than forming a before/after.
datOrderCheck.toolDefect: Died with an unhandled ENOENT on its FIRST default (`build/original/sa`), which the phone never builds, before reaching `game-src/original`, which was present and had the answer. Fixed in 8529c1c6.

ideFlagHistogram.what: Histogram of IDE object-flag bits across every `.ide` under `data/maps`, with example models per bit.
ideFlagHistogram.notAGap: The 14 unread bits are NOT an unhonoured-data finding: plan 039 judged each one — 0x80 is moot (the unlit map never casts, plan 038), 0x1 has no render effect, and the 9/10/11/12/15/16/17/20/22 group is gameplay, skipped by design.
ideFlagHistogram.notAnAB: Plan 039's table cites `scripts/ide-flag-histogram.ts`, a path with ZERO commits in this repository's history. Today's tool is `scripts/debug/ide-flag-histogram.ts`, created whole 2026-07-28, and it walks the `data/maps` FOLDER rather than `gta.dat`'s load list. So this row may not be subtracted from 039's 14 323 defs / bit 0 at 1 937 — two programs, and possibly two trees.

modIdCollisions.what: Which model ids two sources claim with DIFFERENT model names, across stock and every mod.
modIdCollisions.baselineDisagreesWithDoc: docs/debug/README.md records the clean baseline as SEVEN (16700–16708). The eighth is `id 1` — `csplay` against `truth` — outside that range, a cutscene/ped id rather than a LOD rock. Whether `gta.dat` loads either claimant is NOT established, so it is filed as a baseline entry, not a defect.
modIdCollisions.toolDefect: Died with an unhandled ENOENT scandir on `mods-src/original/mods`, which the phone does not carry, throwing away a stock census it had ALREADY computed. Fixed in 8529c1c6; the run above is the verification.

alphaClassCensus.what: What alpha class every texture of an archive gets, and how many the mask rule moves out of the blend pass (plan 092).
alphaClassCensus.archiveIsStockNotBuilt: The tool's OWN default is `build/<game>/sa/models/gta3.img` — the merged, mods-installed tree it calls the closest stand-in for what the pack reads. The phone has no such tree, so its documented fallback to stock was taken. THESE NUMBERS ARE STOCK, and are not the pack's.
alphaClassCensus.readItRight: NOT an optimisation finding. `current` is `classifyAlpha`'s absolute reading; `candidate` is the rule that ALREADY SHIPS, and the shipped classification is their UNION. So 1148 is what the shipped rule already buys, not headroom. What is left in the blend pass is 395 textures of 26 126 (1.5%).
alphaClassCensus.toolWasAlreadyCorrect: Unlike the two tools fixed today, this one resolves its archive through `.find(existsSync)` and throws a readable error naming `--img` when neither candidate exists. It is the model for the rest of the class.

lampCensus.what: Which vehicle models carry the standard lamp material, and which carry ivflights.
lampCensus.archive: game-src/original/models/gta3.img (the stock fallback this fix added)
lampCensus.toolDefect: Died with an unhandled ENOENT on `build/original/opensa/models/gta3.img`, a built tree the phone never produces, while the stock archive sat beside it unread. Fixed in adad4184 with alpha-class-census's resolver; the run above is the verification.

lodLinkCheck.what: Does every LOD link still point at its own LOD? A `lod` cell is a ROW INDEX, so any stage dropping or inserting an `inst` row re-points every link past it at another VALID row.
lodLinkCheck.verdictMatchesDoc: docs/debug/README.md calls stock clean with 0 findings, and `0 out of range` is that verdict. The seven `farther than 20 u` are all `BillBd*` in `law2_stream1.ipl` — stock billboards whose LOD legitimately stands off — and the README already says 20 u is the FLOOR of what the check guarantees, not a defect threshold.
lodLinkCheck.toolWasAlreadyCorrect: Guards `data/gta.dat` under its default and exits 1 with a usage line. No fix needed.

treeDisagreesWithDocBaselines.what: THREE tools now read a different count from the doc for the same path, and the two that are comparable to themselves both read HIGH.

ideFlagHistogram.notComparable: Different program — plan 039's `scripts/ide-flag-histogram.ts` has zero commits in this repository's history. Excluded from the pattern.

treeDisagreesWithDocBaselines.readItRight: Every VERDICT matches the doc (clean is clean). Only the counts move, and both comparable ones move UP, so the phone's `game-src/original` carries slightly MORE than the copy the baselines were taken on. WHAT differs is not established. Until it is, a doc baseline may not be used as a before/after partner for a run on this device.

txdDimensionCensus.what: Raster dimensions across every TXD of a tree: DXT that is not block-aligned (FATAL — never loads and takes its WHOLE dictionary down) and non-power-of-two but aligned (loads).
txdDimensionCensus.fatalClassIsClean: 0 unaligned DXT — the class that silently kills a whole dictionary is clean, and that verdict matches the doc.
txdDimensionCensus.contradictsARestriction: THREE counts in gta3.img disagree with three documented numbers, all in the same direction. (1) The script's own header says `Stock: 26 004 textures, 0 of either`; this tree reads 26 126 and 3. (2) docs/restrictions/README.md states `stock has 0 NPOT` for this class. (3) docs/gta-sa-original/uncompressed-rasters.md states `Every uncompressed raster in the game is single-level`, measured over gta3.img + gta_int.img — and `icons4.txd: diskmetal32` is an UNCOMPRESSED rgba8888 raster with EIGHT mip levels, inside gta3.img, which is inside that measurement's scope. So it is a real counterexample rather than an out-of-scope one.
txdDimensionCensus.crossCheck: 26 126 textures matches alpha-class-census's total exactly, from a different entry point.
txdDimensionCensus.scope: models/gta3.img ONLY — not the whole tree. The 2 760 dictionaries are inside that archive.
txdDimensionCensus.whyNotFiledAsADocDefect: Not corrected in the docs, because the cause is not established and this tree reads HIGH against every baseline (+122 textures here). A raster added to this copy explains all three as easily as a wrong doc does, and nothing separates them yet. Establishing WHAT differs about this game copy settles all of them at once — it is the cheapest next thing in this area.

iplRowCensus.what: What a game costs against SA's permanent-placement ceilings: every text-IPL `inst` row and every gta.dat slot carrying one, including what modloader adds.
iplRowCensus.dir: game-src/original (the phone's real install, a symlink to /storage/emulated/0/Download/New Folder)
iplRowCensus.THIS_IS_THE_ANSWER: The phone's `game-src/original` is a SA-MP INSTALL, not a clean stock copy — its `gta.dat` carries an `IPL SAMP\samp.ipl` line. That is the class of difference behind every count in treeDisagreesWithDocBaselines reading HIGH against a documented 'stock' baseline.
iplRowCensus.whatItDoesNotYetExplain: The SA-MP line itself is UNRESOLVED, so it contributes zero rows — it proves the copy is not stock, it does not arithmetically account for the +138 inst rows over the doc. And modloader added 0, so that is not the source either. WHICH files carry the extra rows is still unlisted.
iplRowCensus.whyItMatters: Twofold. (1) A doc baseline labelled 'stock' is not a partner for any run on this device, which is now established rather than suspected. (2) 202 is a dispatch product FOR a SA-MP server, so the copy this repository's only game-data machine holds is the product's actual target rather than an accident.

carmodsCheck.what: Does this tree's `carmods.dat` name a model no IDE row defines? The real game crashes at boot on one (0x007F0BF7).
carmodsCheck.result: ok — every carmods.dat token has an IDE row
carmodsCheck.whyItMatters: docs/restrictions/assets-and-data.md marks the DECLARED half of this class SILENT: the installer catches inheritance, nothing catches a declared part whose dummy is absent, and ModelVariations spawns traffic tuned so the crash needs nobody to visit a mod shop. Clean on the SA-MP install the phone holds.
carmodsCheck.toolWasAlreadyCorrect: Requires an explicit game dir and refuses without one.

toolsNotRunAndWhy.pak-placement-parity: Skipped deliberately. The phone's pak is built over ONE district (los-santos-centre), so 'uncovered' would be enormous by construction rather than by defect — the script's own header warns that a near-total miss is what a mismatched pair reports. It needs a whole-map pak to mean anything.

twoDfxCensus.what: Which 2dfx entry types the authored models carry, by entries, models and payload size.
twoDfxCensus.scope: openGameArchive('original') — one game archive, not the whole tree.
twoDfxCensus.disagreesWithPlan100: Plan 100 records roadsign as `WORLD, 489 of 489`, and the restriction built on it says 131 of 489 sit outside the cell of the instance carrying them. This tree reads 480. **The direction is OPPOSITE to every other disagreement today**, which all read HIGH — so 'this copy is bigger' does not explain it, and the SA-MP finding is a CLASS of difference rather than a full account. Plan 100 does not state its scan scope, so identical scopes are not established either.
